tracks.narration: There's a way to minimize a Boolean function by drawing — not algebra. Karnaugh maps.
Take a function of three variables — A, B, C — and assume it's one for these six minterms.
Lay out a Karnaugh map: A B down the side in Gray code, C across the top. Drop in a one wherever the function equals one.
Now the magic. Two rectangles cover all six ones. The vertical block is A. The horizontal block is B. Together — A or B.
F equals A or B. Two terms instead of three — and you didn't have to factor anything.
